citations.claim: initial total mechanical energy is 420 J with bodies at rest
energy just before violation is already rising, at 437.8 J
first violating step: energy exceeds initial plus tolerance with no controller work

explanation: Vertical stack of 5 elastic (e=1) bodies under strong gravity (30) with large dt (1/30). Gravity compresses the stack into simultaneous contacts; sequential impulse + positional correction resolves overlaps by pushing bodies apart and flipping velocities upward, injecting kinetic energy faster than gravity removes it. By step 6 energy grows from 420 J to ~505 J with zero controller work, exceeding the 10%+5J bound. Classic contact-solver energy gain in tall elastic stacks.
vision_note: A vertical stack of five blue circles remains in a tight column through steps 3 to 6, settling only slightly downward with no visible separation or explosion. No red violating body, walls, or dramatic motion appears in any tile, so nothing looks energetically wrong. [disagreement: The explanation claims bodies are pushed apart and velocities flip upward injecting large kinetic energy by step 6, but the frames show the stack still compact and stationary with no spreading or upward launch.]
